office: President of the Chicago Board of Education (nonpartisan)
scope_plain: Every Chicago voter. Nonpartisan: no party labels on the ballot.
office_explainer: Runs Chicago school board meetings and votes as a member, with no veto. Elected citywide.
why_it_matters: First time all 21 board seats are elected. The board votes on CPS's nearly $10 billion budget, sets policy and hires the schools chief for about 315,000 students (FOX 32). New terms begin Jan. 15, 2027. Ten district seats get four-year terms and ten get two-year terms this time (WTTW); which is which is not in our sources. Appointed board president Sean Harden is not running (Chalkbeat). Sendhil Revuluri withdrew on Sept. 30 (WTTW) but was on the official candidate list issued Sept. 11, so his name may still appear.

candidates.name: Victor P. Henderson
candidates.background: Attorney whose children attended CPS; has served as an outside ethics officer for the Chicago Housing Authority and counsel to the U.S. House Ethics Committee (campaign biography, via FOX 32).

own_words.text: Says CPS has not managed its finances responsibly and wants to cut "unnecessary, politically-driven costs and bloat" (FOX 32 notes he did not specify which).
Says CPS must "re-commit itself to providing the kind of wraparound services that keep kids safe and nourished."

candidates.name: Jessica Biggs
candidates.background: Current elected board member (District 6B). Former CPS principal (Edmund Burke Elementary, from 2012) and special education teacher.

own_words.text: Campaign priorities: expand preschool access, eliminate racial and socioeconomic inequities, and send a bigger share of district money directly to schools.
Wants a "Springfield strategy with teeth" to win more state funding.

candidates.name: Sendhil Revuluri
candidates.background: Former board vice president, appointed in 2019 by Mayor Lori Lightfoot; former New York teacher who co-founded a public school; works at PEAK6 Capital Management. WITHDREW from the race on Sept. 30, 2026 (WTTW).

own_words.text: Campaign priorities before withdrawing: clear goals for student success, "reality-based" budgeting, and helping families understand the board's work to "build real trust."

candidates.name: Hilario Dominguez
candidates.background: Former special education teacher who has worked as the Chicago Teachers Union's political director (FOX 32, Chalkbeat; the Sun-Times calls him a former CTU deputy political director). Pilsen native and Whitney Young graduate.

own_words.text: Top issues: universal preschool, better meals for students, and more access to jobs and internships.
